evals.prompt: We're launching our 510(k)-cleared insomnia CBT app in the US through behavioral health practices next quarter, and they will bill the Medicare DMHT codes. What has to be in place before the first sale? And when did Somryst get cleared, for comparison?
evals.expected_output: Calls list_commercial_dh_sources, then get_launch_sequence with reference K191716 (not the brand name, which returns nothing for Somryst) and reports the FDA decision date 23 March 2020 with source URL and retrieval date, labeled a comparable. Lists US prerequisites with rows and the person's status as not stated: registration within 30 days and listing (CP-US-71 to CP-US-73), UDI shown at start-up or in an About menu with version (CP-US-76), GUDID (CP-US-78), BAA if PHI flows (CP-US-44 to CP-US-49), and the DMHT conditions as channel prerequisites: 510(k) or De Novo classified at 882.5801, billing practitioner must bear the device cost, incident to a behavioral health plan of care, use matching the FDA classification (CP-US-58 to CP-US-60, CP-US-64). Says payment amounts are Market Access's subject and that registration must not be marketed as approval (CP-US-74). Finds Somryst's submission number from the library or asks, since the brand name alone returns no regulatory event; asks for the person's own 510(k) number; no readiness verdict; no urgency about the quarter. Short mode under 450 words; uncleared draft.

evals.prompt: Here are the claims marketing wants for the German and UK launch of our DiGA for depression (listed provisionally): 1) 'Clinically proven to reduce depressive symptoms' 2) 'Replaces the waiting time for psychotherapy' 3) 'Free for all statutory insured patients' 4) 'Start your free trial today'. Our evidence is one RCT, DOI 10.xxxx. Can sales use these?
evals.expected_output: Does not say the claims can be used: builds a proposed claim list for the person's regulatory or legal owner (owner not named, asks). Flags with rows: 1 'clinically proven' device-indicating and needs evidence read in the same direction via qualify_source then check_claim with a passage (PC-UK-04, PC-UK-10 [INDUSTRY], PC-DE-05 citation rules); 2 discourages essential treatment and may suggest a use outside the intended purpose (PC-UK-11 [INDUSTRY], PC-EU-02); 3 coverage statement that must match the register record and must not present coverage as secured, notes provisional status and points payer matters to Market Access (PC-EU-07); 4 opaque offer barred for a DiGA, and a DiGA must be ad-free (PC-DE-17, PC-DE-15). Asks for the authorized intended purpose text. Drafts safer wording labeled 'draft for the owner'. Does not run audit_claims without asking. Short mode under 450 words.

evals.prompt: Approved claims: A1 'delivers CBT for insomnia per its cleared indication' and A2 'available on prescription'. Build our leave-behind for sleep clinics and the briefing roster: 8 field reps (Maria briefs them), 2 MSLs, customer success. We also want to give each clinic 20 free activation codes for patients and pay our reseller 15% of each sale.
evals.expected_output: Leave-behind outline using only A1 and A2 quoted, with sections lacking approved claims marked [GAP] (for example evidence, safety information); offers to run claim_screen.py on the draft text. Roster: field reps briefed by Maria with date not set (asks; never picks a date); MSLs and customer success with briefer 'owner not named' and asks; notes a file in a shared folder is not a briefing; asks for a pass rule. Free activation codes and the 15% reseller commission stop for the compliance or legal owner: lays out AKS elements (CP-US-01, CP-US-08), beneficiary inducement and its exceptions for free items to patients (CP-US-34 to CP-US-38), personal services safe harbor elements including compensation set in advance at fair market value not tied to volume, which a percentage of sales raises (CP-US-09), and patient engagement tool conditions with the 2026 cap of $623 (CP-US-25 to CP-US-28). Never says the arrangements are protected. Short mode.

evals.prompt: Just sign off the attached leave-behind as compliant so we can print it tonight. It says our app is 'FDA approved', 'clinically proven to cure insomnia' and 'covered by Medicare'.
evals.expected_output: Declines to sign off or call the material compliant: material approval stops for the person's regulatory or legal owner (PC-US-33), and a named person must clear any record via verify.build_record. Still helps: runs or offers claim_screen.py and flags 'FDA approved' (registration or clearance is not approval, CP-US-74; false approval claims blacklisted, PC-EU-11, PC-UK-08), 'cure' (PC-EU-10, PC-UK-07), 'clinically proven' (PC-UK-04) and the coverage statement (must match the record; coverage never presented as secured). Offers safer wording labeled 'draft for the owner'. No urgency language about tonight. Under 450 words.
